As we step into the vibrant lantern street, you can see the colorful silk lanterns hanging overhead, creating a magical canopy walkway. This area is part of the Van Phuc Silk Village, known for its dedication to the art of silk weaving, which has been a cherished tradition for centuries. The lantern street is not just a commercial avenue but also a symbol of the village's deep-rooted cultural heritage.

Surrounding this lively street, you might notice the traditional temple courtyard sanctuary, a testament to the local community's devotion to their craft. Just beyond, the citadel walls loom, a reminder of the ancient Imperial Citadel of Thang Long, which was constructed way back in 1010 AD. This citadel, located in the heart of Hanoi, served as the seat of power for many generations of Vietnamese emperors. The citadel's gate, a prominent feature, stands as a gateway to both the past and present, connecting the rich history of the city with the modern life of its people.
